newsitem.title: USA: Leucadia sees gain from Colonial Penn sale.
newsitem.headline: Leucadia sees gain from Colonial Penn sale.

text.p: Leucadia National Corp said on Monday it expects to report a pre-tax gain of about $600 million upon the completion of the sale of its Colonial Penn P&C Group to GE Capital Corp.
The company said it may record the gain in either the third or fourth quarters of 1997.
Leucadia said it agreed to sell Colonial Penn, a direct marketer of personal auto insurance, to GE Capital Corp for $950 million cash.
The transaction, which is subject to Leucadia shareholder approval and regulatory approvals, is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 1997.

The terms of the transaction call for 1997 earnings to remain in the Colonial Penn P&C Group, with GE Capital paying interest on the purchase price at a rate of 6 percent a year from January 1, 1997 to closing.
For calendar 1996, the Colonial Penn P&C Group had revenues of about $596 million and pre-tax earnings of about $73 million.

The Colonial Penn P&C Group consists of Colonial Penn Insurance Co, Colonial Penn Madison Insurance Co, Colonial Penn Franklin Insurance Co, Bayside Casualty Insurance Co, and Bay Colony Insurance Co.
In late April, Leucadia agreed to sell its Colonial Penn Life Insurance Co and Providential Life Insurance Co to Conseco Inc for $460 million.
Those two transactions followed a statement by the company in early April that several companies had expressed interest in the acquisition of certain of its insurance operations.
The company did not say, at that time, which of its insurance operations had attracted interest from potential buyers.
But the company on Monday said it was referring to the two Colonial Penn insurance businesses in that April statement.

The company's remaining insurance operations consist of personal and commercial property and casualty insurer Empire Group and the variable annuity business conducted through Charter National Life Insurance Co and Intramerica Life Insurance Co.
The company said it had no near-term plans to exit the remaining insurance businesses.
